newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan army puts end to oil refinery protest.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan army puts end to oil refinery protest.

text.p: A five-day occupation that halted production at Guatemala's only crude oil refinery ended on Tuesday when the army removed some 300 protesters demanding back pay for helping the government fight rebels.
"They were peacefully removed by security forces, the national police and the army," Nery Morales, spokesman for the Interior Ministry, told Reuters.

The Basic Resources International Ltd. plant in the northern Peten region was shut down for five consecutive days. The protest may have spurred a shutdown of the nation's entire output of 23,000 barrels per day (bpd), sources said.
Guatemala's refined products are exported. Basic officials were not available to comment on the impact of the five-day halt in exports.

Protesting former paramilitary patrolmen were demanding payment for their role in a 36-year civil war that ended with the signing of a peace treaty last December. Government officials have said they will not reimburse any patrolmen.
Since the peace treaty, former patrols have occupied the Basic plant three times to demand pay for helping the army.

The patrolmen were armed by the military and hired to spy on suspected guerrilla sympathizers in rural towns and also came under intense criticism from human rights groups. They said they were not paid for their activities.
The ministry's Morales said a presidential commission had agreed to reopen talks with the patrolmen who had occupied the refinery.
